title: Time on a video reads in frames where an editor expects frames
goal: A Premiere or Final Cut editor thinks in frames: they trim a transition to 12 frames and park the playhead at 00:00:04:12. Photonz says 0:04 on the transport and 0.8s beside a transition you drag, so an editor cannot land on a frame they can name. Show time the way an editor reads it wherever a length or a position is set by hand.
notes: Seen twice now, so it is filed. First: docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md, 'Seen, not filed: No frames in the time readout. The transport says 0:04 and the ruler counts seconds; Premiere shows 00:00:04:12.' Second: queue/audits/2026-09-29-transition-edge-follows-the-pointer.json rough list: 'The bubble shows tenths of a second (0.8s), and hundredths only once the ruler is zoomed in far enough. It does not show frames.' Serves the video-beats-premiere success criterion that the ruler, playhead, clips and captions agree to the frame at every zoom. Update the gap report's line when this closes.
acceptance: Reproduced first: the transport readout, the ruler at its closest zoom and a transition's length bubble are photographed at Next defaults and what each says is written in the log
Whether frames show everywhere or behind a choice (Premiere offers one) is put to the user on a decision card with pictures of both before anything visible changes
Once answered: the transport, the ruler's closest labels, the transition length bubble and the panel's Length row all say the same time for the same moment, to the frame
Typing a length in frames (12) or in timecode (00:00:00:12) into a length field gives the same result
A walk at Next defaults drags a transition to a whole number of frames and reads it back from the bubble and the panel

log.note: Reproduced 2026-10-02 at Next defaults, nothing switched on. Screen locked, so the new lock-safe walk Scripts/playtest/time-reads-today-walk.json took the pictures: transport reads '0:04' (length '0:08'), the ruler at its closest zoom labels '3.9s · 4s · 4.1s', and the timeline bar's zoom readout says '0:03 to 0:04'. Transition bubble: transition-edge-follows-the-pointer-walk's 2-end-mid-drag-sc.png from 2026-10-01 11:01 (no change to ClipTransitionEdgeDrag/ClipTransitions/transport since then) shows bubble '0.8s', panel Length '0.8s', Paid with '0.4s + 0.4s of spare', transport '0:07', edit point 'at 0:07', ruler '0s 3s 6s 9s 12s'. Nothing shows frames.

Adversarial pre-build: the mocks (video-transition-wt, video.html) draw seconds everywhere ('1.0s', '0:18'), so frames by default departs from the floor and is the user's call; Premiere offers Display Format as a choice. Any build also needs: frame rate per clip (VideoExporter already reads nominalFrameRate, default 30), drags snapping to whole frames, length fields parsing '12f' and '00:00:00:12', and every second-based formatter (ClipTransitions.seconds, ClipTransitionCopy.dragReadout, EditorState+Time, VideoEditorView, ruler labels, zoom readout) routed through one time formatter in PhotonzCore. Timecode in the transport takes about 170pt from the scrub bar.

Decision card opened with pictures of today, A (timecode everywhere) and B (seconds default, View > Time Display > Timecode), plus C declining. Pictures are real captures with the numbers painted over, saved beside the brief in queue/decisions/. Recommended B. Nothing visible changed.

Reproduced at Next defaults (transport 0:04, closest ruler 3.9s/4s/4.1s, bubble and Length 0.8s; no frames anywhere). Waiting on the user: timecode everywhere, or seconds by default with View > Time Display > Timecode (recommended). Card has pictures of each.
